66473-arthur.description: A book by Francis A. Niccolls & Co.. It was towards the middle of the month of May, a delicious morning, cooled by a gentle northerly breeze. The roads, deep with a sand as yellow as ochre, though detestable for carriages, which would sink in to the hubs of the wheels, were not at all bad for horseback riding. The farther I advanced towards the interior of the uncultivated and wild country, the more nature became grand and majestic, though perhaps at the same time somewhat monotonous.

arxiv-2212-06905.title: Query Time Optimized Deep Learning Based Video Inference System
arxiv-2212-06905.creator: Mingren Shen, Shuoxuan Dong, Xiuyuan He
arxiv-2212-06905.description: Abstract This is a project report about how we tune Focus [ 1 ] , a video inference system that provides low cost and low latency, through two phases. In this report, we will decrease the query time by saving the middle layer output of the neural network.

arxiv-2504-13691.title: MEGA: Second-Order Gradient Alignment for Catastrophic Forgetting Mitigation in GFSCIL CCS: Mathematics of computing Graph algorithms CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks
arxiv-2504-13691.creator: Jinhui Pang, Changqing Lin, Hao Lin, Jinglin He, Zhengjun Li, Zhihui Zhang, Xiaoshuai Hao
arxiv-2504-13691.description: Abstract . Graph Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (GFSCIL) enables models to continually learn from limited samples of novel tasks after initial training on a large base dataset. Existing GFSCIL approaches typically utilize Prototypical Networks (PNs) for metric-based class representations and fine-tune the model during the incremental learning stage.

arxiv-2510-08199.title: Pursuing decarbonization and competitiveness: a narrow corridor for European green industrial transformation
arxiv-2510-08199.creator: Alice Di Bella, Toni Seibold, Tom Brown, Massimo Tavoni
arxiv-2510-08199.description: Abstract Decarbonizing the industrial sector while maintaining competitiveness are two central objectives of European Union policy, but they can come into conflict. This study examines trade-offs between these goals across two divergent industrial development scenarios in Europe: one marked by a continued decline in industrial production, and another driven by competitiveness-enhancing policies that stimulate a resurgence of industrial activity.

arxiv-2510-13414.title: Mechanizing Olver’s Error Arithmetic
arxiv-2510-13414.creator: Max Fan, Ariel E. Kellison, Samuel D. Pollard
arxiv-2510-13414.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Max Fan, Ariel E. Kellison, Samuel D. Pollard. We mechanize the fundamental properties of a rounding error model for floating-point arithmetic based on relative precision , a measure of error proposed as a substitute for relative error in rounding error analysis. A key property of relative precision is that it forms a true metric, providing a well-defined measure of distance between exact results and their floating-point approximations while offering a structured approach to propagating error bounds through sequences of computations.

arxiv-2512-24058.title: Beyond Hallucinations: A Composite Score for Measuring Reliability in Open-Source Large Language Models
arxiv-2512-24058.creator: Rohit Kumar Salla, Manoj Saravanan, Shrikar Reddy Kota
arxiv-2512-24058.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) like LLaMA, Mistral, and Gemma are increasingly used in decision-critical domains such as healthcare, law, and finance, yet their reliability remains uncertain. They often make overconfident errors, degrade under input shifts, and lack clear uncertainty estimates. Existing evaluations are fragmented, addressing only isolated aspects.

arxiv-2601-17749.title: Over-The-Air Extreme Learning Machines with XL Reception via Nonlinear Cascaded Metasurfaces
arxiv-2601-17749.creator: Kyriakos Stylianopoulos 1 , Mattia Fabiani 2 3 , Giulia Torcolacci 2 3 , Davide Dardari 2 3 , and George C. Alexandropoulos 1
arxiv-2601-17749.description: Abstract The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm calls for the application of inference on wirelessly transferred data via Machine Learning (ML) tools. An emerging research direction deals with the realization of inference ML models directly in the physical layer of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, which, however, entails certain significant challenges.

pmc-10745007.title: Analysis of Factors Affecting the Preparation of Mullite Whiskers from Silica-Rich Slag and Application Studies
pmc-10745007.creator: Shangwen Zhu, Xiaohua Gu, Siwen Liu, Yan Liu, Alexander A Lebedev
pmc-10745007.description: This paper presents an in-depth comparative study of the effects of different molten salt systems, catalyst additions, preparation temperatures, temperature rise rates, and holding times on the properties of mullite whiskers during their preparation process, as well as exploring the enhancement of the toughening effect of mullite whiskers on ceramics.

pmc-11393852.title: Optimization of Vitamin B1, B2, and B6 Absorption in Nang Tay Dum Floating Rice Grains
pmc-11393852.creator: Thi Thao Loan Nguyen, Thi Mong Nghi Pham, Thanh Binh Ho, Binh Ly-Nguyen
pmc-11393852.description: As reported by the FAO, in 2022, approximately 735 million people experienced undernourishment, underscoring the critical need for effective strategies to address micronutrient deficiencies. Among these strategies, the mass fortification of staple foods, particularly rice—a dietary staple for half of the global population—has emerged as one of the most effective approaches.

pmc-11414874.title: PQR cascade: A system proposed for research prioritization in applied sciences
pmc-11414874.creator: Hassan Rafiey, Ameneh S. Forouzan, Sina Ahmadi
pmc-11414874.description: earch and integrating priority setting into research policies are essential for research macro-planning. Yet, a reasonable foundation for prioritization requires trustworthy information and an analytical vision, along with sound reasoning and judgment. Research prioritization is a key process in research management that guarantees the allocation of essentially limited resources and addresses domains conferring the greatest benefits to society.

pmc-11458412.title: Regional diversity in drug-induced lung diseases among the USA, European Union, and Japan
pmc-11458412.creator: Jun Sato, Ryo Sadachi, Takafumi Koyama, Yuki Katsuya, Mao Okada, Noboru Yamamoto
pmc-11458412.description: BackgroundDrug-induced lung disease (DILD) is a considerable and potentially fatal adverse event with poorly understood risk factors. Large-scale, data-driven analyses investigating regional discrepancies in DILD incidence are lacking. The aim of this study was to investigate the potential association among DILD prevalence, regional differences and other factors based on large-scale data base.

pmc-11576129.title: Air pollutants as modulators of mitochondrial quality control in cardiovascular disease
pmc-11576129.creator: Kit Neikirk, Chanel Harris, Han Le, Ashton Oliver, Bryanna Shao, Kaihua Liu, Heather K Beasley, Sydney Jamison, Jeanne A Ishimwe, Annet Kirabo, Antentor Hinton
pmc-11576129.description: It is important to understand the effects of environmental factors such as air pollution on mitochondrial structure and function, especially when these changes increase cardiovascular disease risk. pmc-11608770.title: Sub‐Acromioclavicular Decompression Increases the Risk of Postoperative Shoulder Stiffness after Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair
pmc-11608770.creator: Cheng Li, Zhiling Wang, Maslah Idiris Ali, Yi Long, Ymuhanmode Alike, Min Zhou, Dedong Cui, Zhenze Zheng, Ke Meng, Jingyi Hou, Rui Yang
pmc-11608770.description: ObjectiveThe sub‐acromioclavicular (SAC) decompression is often performed during arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. However, the impact of SAC decompression on patients with postoperative shoulder stiffness (POSS) are controversial and unclear. This study is aim to evaluate the impact of additional sub‐acromioclavicular (SAC) decompression during arthroscopic rotator cuff repair on the postoperative shoulder stiffness (POSS) in patients.

pmc-11977706.title: Disparities in nitrogen and phosphorus management across time and space: a case study of the Chesapeake Bay using the CAFE framework
pmc-11977706.creator: Tan Zou, Eric A Davidson, Robert D Sabo, Graham K MacDonald, Xin Zhang
pmc-11977706.description: Efficient management of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) is imperative for sustainable agriculture, resource conservation, and reducing environmental pollution. Despite progress in on-farm practices and urban wastewater treatment in the Chesapeake Bay (CB) watershed, limited attention has been given to nutrient transport, use, and handling between farms and urban environments.

pmc-12528723.title: A novel integrated framework for damage detection in steel structures using magnetic piezoelectric sensors and hybrid damage index
pmc-12528723.creator: Dattar Singh Aulakh, Divya Rawat, Suresh Bhalla
pmc-12528723.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Electro-mechanical impedance (EMI) and the vibration-based monitoring techniques deploy piezoelectric sensors that are permanently bonded to the structural surface. This increases the risk of sensor degradation over time and raises monitoring costs due to the need for multiple sensors. This study explores the development and performance of reusable single magnet-bonded piezoelectric sensor (MBPS) for damage monitoring in steel structures to address these limitations.

pmc-12649327.title: Fair Treatment and Job Satisfaction: A Multilevel Analysis of Employment Transition
pmc-12649327.creator: Hyunmin Cho, Kyujun Cho, Heungjun Jung, Bereket Kebede, Andy Smith
pmc-12649327.description: Drawing on organizational justice theory, this study examines how workers’ perceptions of fair treatment influence job satisfaction following the transition from temporary agency employment at subcontracting firms to regular employment with client firms. A multilevel analysis was conducted to simultaneously assess individual- and organizational-level effects.

pmc-13301783.title: Ablation of persistent and long-standing persistent AF: beyond pulmonary vein isolations with a novel balloon-in-basket pulsed-field ablation catheter
pmc-13301783.creator: M Wojcik, P Blaszkiewicz
pmc-13301783.description: IntroductionA novel balloon-in-basket catheter (BiBC) has been validated for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but scarce data exist on its use beyond PVI in patients with persistent (PAF) and long-standing persistent (LSPAF) atrial fibrillation (AF) [1-4].PurposeWe hypothesised that BiBC, with its mapping, pacing and pulsed field ablation (PFA) capability, might be use for individualised ablation in PAF nad LSPAF patients.

pmc-13323053.title: Epistatic interactions inform rational design of synthetic microbial communities for bioremediation
pmc-13323053.creator: Mahmoud Yousef, Kiseok Keith Lee, Junivere Tang, Paige Mullen, Vasileios Charisopoulos, Rebecca Willett, Seppe Kuehn
pmc-13323053.description: The metabolism of microbial communities is essential for host and environmental health. The rational design of microbiomes with targeted functional properties is an important objective but remains challenging due to complex interactions and environmental heterogeneity. Community–function landscapes address this challenge by statistically inferring impacts of species presence or absence on function.

pmc-13427492.title: Multiplex PCR for the differentiation of Simulium asakoae and molecular detection of pathogens in the S. asakoae species group in Thailand
pmc-13427492.creator: Kittipat Aupalee, Wichai Srisuka, Hiroyuki Takaoka, Rutchanee Rodpai, Megan Olivia Jones, Kevin Charoenvilaisiri, Jassada Saingamsook, Kanchon Pusawang, Atiporn Saeung
pmc-13427492.description: A human-biting black fly, Simulium (Gomphostilbia) asakoae Takaoka & Davies, 1995, together with certain other members of the S. asakoae species group, is of medical and veterinary importance as a vector of various pathogens. However, accurate species identification remains challenging due to the high morphological similarity among related members and the limitations of cox1 barcoding.

pmc-13613422.title: Methodological Considerations Regarding the Comparison of Clevidipine and Nicardipine in Hypertensive Emergencies
pmc-13613422.creator: Shuai Zhang, Yishuo Zhang
pmc-13613422.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). on that the two agents perform comparably on most efficacy and safety endpoints is broadly consistent with an earlier meta‐analysis restricted to cerebrovascular populations [2]. Several methodological aspects, however, deserve closer attention before these findings inform treatment choices. First, eight of the nine included studies were retrospective, and pooling them with the single randomized trial in one random‐effects model may overstate the certainty of the pooled estimates.

pmc-13700182.title: Life satisfaction in later life: the role of economic security, health, and religious belief among urban Iranian older adults
pmc-13700182.creator: Fardin Alipour, Toktam Paykani, Hassan Rafiey, Meroe Vameghi, Shekoufeh Ahmadi, Vahid Rashedi
pmc-13700182.description: IntroductionLife satisfaction in later adulthood is a central indicator of successful aging and reflects the overall evaluation individuals make of their quality of life. Previous research suggests that subjective well-being in older age is shaped by a combination of socioeconomic conditions, physical health, and psychosocial or cultural factors.
